stories.title: Nobel Prize in Medicine 2026: trio honoured for optogenetics
stories.body: the Nobel Assembly at Sweden's Karolinska Institute announced on 5 October that the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine goes to Karl Deisseroth (54, American, Stanford University), Peter Hegemann (71, German) and Georg Nagel (73, German) for "discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics". The breakthrough: Hegemann and Nagel discovered channelrhodopsin, a light-sensitive protein in the alga Chlamydomonas that opens an ion channel when exposed to light; Deisseroth then engineered nerve cells to produce it, so blue light can switch individual nerve cells on or off inside a living brain — the technique, named optogenetics in 2006, is now used in laboratories worldwide to map the neural circuits behind memory, feelings and behaviour, and to study neurological and psychiatric disorders. The three share 12 million Swedish kronor (~US$1.2 million).

stories.title: India–Switzerland sign migration and mobility partnership pact
stories.body: following the wide-ranging talks between PM Narendra Modi and Swiss President Guy Parmelin (day 1 of his 5–7 Oct state visit, New Delhi, 5 October), the two countries signed a migration and mobility partnership pact, decided to expand Swiss market access for Indian exports, and agreed to further deepen cooperation in nuclear energy and defence — with the agenda also covering trade and investment, and critical technologies. The visit marks one year of the India–EFTA TEPA (EFTA = Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein; USD 100 billion investment target over 15 years), and Parmelin participates in the 2nd India–EFTA Prosperity Summit on 7 October.

stories.title: CJI Surya Kant: SC did not approve "any" Form 6 modifications
stories.body: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant stated that the Supreme Court had not approved "any" modifications to Form 6 (the form voters must fill), while a three-judge bench headed by him heard the petitions filed against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar — amid the Congress's agitation over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and its demand for action against the CEC.

stories.title: Jaishankar: India in talks with Russia and Ukraine to help end the war
stories.body: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, speaking at the Munich Leaders' Meeting in New Delhi, said India is in talks with both Russia and Ukraine to help end the war that started in February 2022 — with discussions covering Black Sea shipping, grain and energy exports, and avoiding attacks.

stories.title: Army's Exercise Jai Se Vijay: highway helicopter landings near the Pakistan border
stories.body: the Indian Army conducted Exercise Jai Se Vijay on 29 September near Dantour in Rajasthan's Bikaner district (~80 km from the India–Pakistan International Border), turning a stretch of National Highway-911 into a temporary helicopter landing zone. Army Aviation units of the South Western Command (Sapta Shakti Command) carried out landing and take-off drills with Rudra, Dhruv and Chetak helicopters — showcasing the military value of dual-use highway infrastructure in border areas where fixed airfields are limited.

stories.title: 150 illegal Bangladeshi immigrants in J&K being deported
stories.body: Jammu and Kashmir authorities said on 5 October that 150 Bangladeshi nationals living illegally in the Union Territory were being deported.

stories.title: KAZIND-2026: 9th edition underway in Kazakhstan
stories.body: India and Kazakhstan are conducting the ninth edition of the joint military exercise KAZIND-2026 from 28 September to 11 October 2026 in Oskemen, Kazakhstan.

stories.title: RBI's draft foreign investment rules put AIFs in the spotlight
stories.body: the draft FEMA (Foreign Investment) Rules, 2026, released by the RBI on 21 July 2026 to replace the NDI Rules, 2019, propose treating Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) with over 50% non-resident interest as indirect foreign investment — closing what SEBI and the RBI see as regulatory arbitrage, where foreign investors use domestically managed AIFs to bypass FDI sectoral caps. Under the NDI Rules, an AIF counted as domestic if its sponsor and investment manager were Indian-owned and controlled; the draft introduces the concept of a foreign-controlled entity (FCE) but lacks AIF-specific ownership/control tests — prompting PE/VC funds to warn it could hurt capital inflows and asking for the status quo.

stories.title: SEBI chief warns investors against anonymous tips and unrealistic returns
stories.body: cautioning retail investors to stay away from anonymous investment tips and promises of unrealistic returns.

stories.title: IndiGo raises fuel surcharge on domestic and international flights
stories.body: the airline introduced a new fuel surcharge of up to ₹6,000 on international routes (with higher charges on domestic flights too) to pass on rising fuel costs.

stories.title: Kerala to launch IT Parks Affiliation Scheme today (6 Oct)
stories.body: the state will launch a scheme to connect IT companies outside major government-owned IT parks with Kerala's state-level technology ecosystem.

stories.title: Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 2026
stories.body: the new Act, which recently came into force, replaced the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891.

stories.title: IOA's new awards: Kumkum Mohod and Sujeet Kalkal are the first recipients
stories.body: the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) announced on 4 October that archer Kumkum Mohod (17) and wrestler Sujeet Kalkal will be the first recipients of the newly instituted Jaspal Rana Award (best female sportsperson of the Asian Games) and Raja Randhir Singh Award (best male sportsperson) for their gold-winning performances at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026. The awards honour the legacies of Jaspal Rana (legendary shooter, 8 Asian Games medals including 4 gold) and Raja Randhir Singh (renowned shooter and sports administrator, 4 Asian Games medals including 1 gold) — both passed away earlier this year.

stories.title: IOAA 2026: India wins 4 gold + 1 silver, finishes joint third
stories.body: the Indian team won four gold and one silver at the 19th International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics (IOAA), held in Hanoi, Vietnam, 25 September – 5 October — the largest IOAA ever, with 307 students from 64 countries. Gold medallists: Pranjal Dixit (Hyderabad), Sumant Gupta (Delhi), Akshat Srivastava (Gurugram), Arnav Sehrawat (Faridabad); silver: Harshil Amitkumar Patel (Vadodara). India finished joint third with Vietnam, behind Iran and South Korea (five golds each). The results also complete a historic clean sweep: with all senior Olympiads (Maths, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Astronomy) done, every Indian student this year won gold (16) or silver (8) — a first since 1989.
